best_for: People who want a small, ad-free BitTorrent client on a Mac, PC or Linux box, or a headless one on a home server or NAS.
description:
Transmission is a free BitTorrent client for downloading and sharing files over the torrent network. It is open source under the GPL and built by volunteers, and the project says it does not track its users. Ubuntu picked it as its default torrent app, and Western Digital, Zyxel and Belkin have used it in their devices.

The defaults work as they are, so you can open a torrent and start downloading without changing a thing. If you want to drive it from somewhere else, other people have written add-ons for it: remote controls for Android and iOS, browser-based control panels, a Telegram bot, and FlexGet for picking up new torrents from RSS feeds. The project points out it does not support those add-ons itself.

points.title: No ads, no bundles, no paid tier
points.text: Transmission is free and open source, run by volunteers. There are no toolbars, pop-ups or bundled extras, and every feature is in the one free version.

points.title: Light enough for a NAS
points.text: It is built to use little memory, so it suits home servers. A headless daemon, a web interface and the `transmission-remote` command let you control it from another machine.

points.title: A native app on each system
points.text: The Mac app is native and Apple silicon ready, Linux has GTK and Qt apps, and Windows uses a Qt app.

points.title: Useful extras built in
points.text: It has watch folders, a blocklist for bad peers, tracker editing and speed limits. The project publishes SHA256 hashes and code-signed Windows installers so you can check your download.

points.title: Windows 10 for the main builds
points.text: The standard MSI installers need Windows 10 or later; Qt5 builds remain for Windows 7. The Mac app needs macOS 12 or later.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is a community build
points.text: The project calls the Flathub package a community package, and Flathub does not mark it as verified. Most distributions also carry Transmission in their own repositories.

points.title: Downgrades on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 10 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release; the project keeps older releases on GitHub.
